    tempest_fastapi_sdk.admin¶

    O painel admin estilo Django: site, model admin, ações, políticas de acesso, auditoria e páginas.

    « Admin, dados e API

    AdminSite ¶

    AdminSite(
    title: str = "Admin",
    *,
    brand: str | None = None,
    index_subtitle: str | None = None,
    site_url: str | None = None,
    theme: AdminTheme | None = None,
    dashboard_cards: Sequence[MetricCard] = (),
    display_timezone: str | None = None,
    metrics_areas: Sequence[MetricsArea] = (),
    location_maps: Sequence[BRLocationMap] = (),
    locale: AdminLocale = DEFAULT_ADMIN_LOCALE,
    recent_activity: int | None = None,
)

    Holds the set of :class:AdminModel configurations to expose.

    Each project instantiates one site, registers its admin configurations (one at a time with :meth:register, or all at once with :meth:automap), and passes the site to :func:make_admin_router.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    title str

    Branding shown in the page <title> and the dashboard heading.
    brand str | None

    Optional override for the centered header brand text. Falls back to :attr:title when unset — read it through :attr:brand_text.
    index_subtitle str

    Optional subtitle for the dashboard.
    site_url str | None

    Optional "View site" link rendered in the admin header.
    theme AdminTheme

    Typed appearance overrides (colors, logo, favicon, font, footer, dark mode). Defaults to a stock :class:AdminTheme, so the look is unchanged when omitted.
    dashboard_cards list[MetricCard]

    Business-metric cards (value / trend / partition) rendered at the top of the dashboard, each computed from the DB on load. Distinct from the system CPU/RAM/disk panel.
    metrics_areas list[MetricsArea]

    Indicator pages generated from a schema and a service, one card per field.
    location_maps list[BRLocationMap]

    Map pages of where a model's rows are in Brazil.
    locale AdminLocale

    Language of the panel's own text.
    recent_activity int | None

    Entries of the dashboard's recent activity feed, or None when the feed is off.

    Initialize the site.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    title str

    Branding text — used in the page <title> and the dashboard heading.

    		 'Admin'
    brand str | None

    Optional text for the centered header brand. None (default) falls back to title, so existing sites keep their current header. Set it to show a distinct name (e.g. "servus-backend-admin") centered at the top of every page.

    		 None
    index_subtitle str | None

    Dashboard and login subtitle. None (default) uses the catalog's "Site administration" in :attr:locale.

    		 None
    site_url str | None

    Optional outbound link rendered in the admin header.

    		 None
    theme AdminTheme | None

    Typed appearance overrides. None (default) uses a stock :class:AdminTheme, leaving the look identical to earlier versions.

    		 None
    dashboard_cards Sequence[MetricCard]

    Business-metric cards rendered on the dashboard.

    		 ()
    display_timezone str | None

    IANA zone every registered model inherits for its datetime columns — the zone the operator reads and types in. A model that declares its own keeps it. None (default) leaves everything in UTC. The zone belongs to the panel rather than to any one table, which is why it is settable here instead of being repeated on every :class:AdminModel.

    		 None
    metrics_areas Sequence[MetricsArea]

    Indicator pages, each generated from a schema and a service method with no arguments, listed under "Metrics" in the sidebar. Gated by the METRICS surface.

    		 ()
    location_maps Sequence[BRLocationMap]

    Map pages listed under "Maps" in the sidebar, each shading Brazil by a model's row count per state. Gated by VIEW on that model.

    		 ()
    locale AdminLocale

    Language of the panel's own text — labels, buttons, empty states, flash messages and the errors the router renders (see :mod:tempest_fastapi_sdk.admin.i18n). "en" (default) keeps the strings the panel always had; "pt-BR" renders Brazilian Portuguese. Text you configure (model and field names, verbose_name, action labels, title) is shown as given.

    		 DEFAULT_ADMIN_LOCALE
    recent_activity int | None

    Show the last N changes of every registered model that declares audit_model on the dashboard, merged newest first, each linking to its row. None (default) leaves the feed off, because it costs queries on every dashboard load: one per audit table, one per audited model to keep only the rows the principal reaches, and one author lookup per distinct author. A model the principal may not VIEW is left out, and so is an entry whose row falls outside the model's row_scope (or no longer exists, on a scoped model), label included.

    		 None

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValueError

    When display_timezone is not a zone the host's tz database knows, or two metrics_areas (or two location_maps) share a URL slug, or locale is not one of :data:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.admin.i18n.ADMIN_LOCALES, or recent_activity is not a positive number.

    automap ¶

    automap(
    source: str | ModuleType,
    *,
    exclude: Sequence[type[BaseModel] | str] = (),
    skip_registered: bool = True,
    **admin_kwargs: Any,
) -> list[AdminModel[Any]]

    Register every concrete model found under source at once.

    The batch counterpart to :meth:register: instead of writing one site.register(AdminModel(model=...)) per table, point this at the package that holds the ORM models and every concrete :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.BaseModel subclass is wrapped in a default :class:AdminModel and registered.

    Example::

    site = AdminSite(title="Servus", brand="servus-backend-admin")
site.automap("src.db.models")

    Abstract bases (BaseUserModel and friends — no __tablename__) are skipped automatically. Models you want configured by hand can be registered first and left out here with skip_registered=True (the default), or hidden entirely via exclude.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    source str | ModuleType

    Dotted module path (e.g. "src.db.models") or an already-imported module/package. Packages have their submodules swept too.

    		 required
    exclude Sequence[type[BaseModel] | str]

    Models to skip — each entry is the model class, its class name, or its table name.

    		 ()
    skip_registered bool

    When True (default), a model whose slug is already registered is left untouched, so you can register a hand-tuned AdminModel first and let automap fill in the rest. When False, a collision raises ValueError (as :meth:register does).

    		 True
    **admin_kwargs Any

    Forwarded to every AdminModel constructed here (e.g. page_size=50, can_delete=False). Applied uniformly — reach for per-model :meth:register when a model needs its own configuration.

    		 {}

    Returns:

    Type Description
    list[AdminModel[Any]]

    list[AdminModel[Any]]: The admins newly registered by this
    list[AdminModel[Any]]

    call, ordered by table name.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValueError

    When skip_registered is False and a discovered model's slug is already registered.

    model: type[ModelT],

    Bases: Generic[ModelT]

    Declarative admin configuration for one SQLAlchemy model.

    Instantiate once per managed model and pass it to :meth:AdminSite.register. Unlike Django's class-based ModelAdmin, this is a plain typed instance — the constructor signature is the contract, fields accept real SQLAlchemy column attributes (so typos surface in the editor, not at runtime), and there is no metaclass magic::

    site.register(AdminModel(
    model=UserModel,
    list_display=[UserModel.email, UserModel.is_admin],
    search_fields=[UserModel.email],
    ordering=desc(UserModel.created_at),
))

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default

    The SQLAlchemy model class.

    		 required

    Columns shown in the list view. None defaults to every column except the password hash.

    		 None

    Fields surfaced as filter dropdowns; matched via the repository's standard filter pipeline.

    		 ()

    Text columns the list's search box (?q=) and the export look in. Each word of the term is an escaped, case-insensitive ILIKE %word% ORed across these columns, and every word must match in some column; % and _ are literal. The first entry also labels the row in FK selects and autocomplete.

    		 ()

    		 ()

    		 None

    A create flow driven by a schema and a service instead of the columns (an API key minted and shown once). "+ New" opens the schema's form. Mutually exclusive with can_create=True.

    		 None

    Whether the admin exposes the edit form + POST endpoint. Default True.

    		 True

    Whether the admin exposes the delete action. Default True.

    		 True

    Whether the list view offers the built-in "Activate" / "Deactivate" bulk actions (they also need can_edit). False hides them and refuses a forged submission — for tables where is_active carries no meaning, such as a payout ledger. Default True.

    		 True
    can_import bool

    Whether the admin exposes a CSV import page (GET/POST {prefix}/m/{slug}/import) that bulk-creates rows from an uploaded CSV. Default False (opt-in); also requires can_create.

    		 False
    actions Sequence[AnyActionHandler]

    Custom bulk actions — functions decorated with :func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.admin.admin_action. Each appears in the list view's bulk-action dropdown alongside the built-in activate / deactivate / delete; an action_policy on :func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.admin.make_admin_router decides, per action, who sees and runs it.

    		 ()
    upload_fields Sequence[FieldRef]

    String columns rendered as file inputs in the create/edit form. The uploaded file is saved through upload_storage and the returned storage key is written to the column.

    		 ()
    upload_storage UploadStorage | None

    Backend used to persist uploaded files (LocalUploadStorage / MinIOUploadStorage). Required when upload_fields is non-empty.

    		 None
    upload_accept Mapping[FieldRef, Sequence[str]] | None

    MIME types an upload field takes ({"receipt_key": ["application/pdf"]}). The input gets accept=, and a submission is refused with a field error unless the declared type is listed and, when the list holds any type :func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.sniff_mime recognises (:data:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.utils.SNIFFABLE_MIMETYPES), the leading bytes sniff as a listed type — a PNG renamed .pdf is refused. The check is per list, not per type: mixing text/plain with application/pdf refuses plain text, since text has no signature to sniff. A field left out accepts anything, as before.

    		 None
    validate_edit EditValidator | None

    Called on an edit submission with the stored row and the posted form, before any upload is written; a non-empty {field: message} refuses the save with those errors. For a rule that depends on the row's state, such as a receipt that cannot change once the row is final.

    		 None
    readonly_fields_for ReadonlyFieldsFor | None

    Called with the stored row when its edit form is rendered and when it is submitted; the columns it returns are locked for that row on top of readonly_fields, the same way: left out of the edit form, and a value posted for them is ignored on save. For a column editable only while the row is in some state, such as a reason that freezes once the row is final. It covers the columns the form parses — upload and password fields are handled apart, so lock those with validate_edit — and the row's own edit form, not an inline formset.

    		 None
    audit_model type[BaseAuditLogModel] | None

    When set, the detail view renders a per-row change timeline read from this audit table (matched on entity = the model name and entity_id = the row id). Pair it with BaseRepository(audit_model=...) + add_audited / update_audited / delete_audited so the history is actually written. None (default) shows only the created_by / updated_by stamps.

    		 None
    choices Mapping[FieldRef, ChoiceSource]

    Columns rendered as a <select> of fixed values although the column itself is a plain String — an enum stored as text, or an open vocabulary the admin should still restrict. Each value is an Enum class (its values, labelled from the member names), a sequence of strings, or of (value, label) pairs. The form shows the select and the submission is refused with a field error when the value is not in the list. A column that is also in list_filter gets the same select (with the same labels) as its list filter instead of a free-text box. A real enum column (Mapped[MyEnum]) is a select already and needs no entry.

    		 None
    autocomplete_fields Sequence[FieldRef]

    Foreign-key columns rendered as a typed search box (HTMX) instead of a <select> of every related row — removing the 1000-row cap and the plain-UUID fallback for large target tables. The target table must have its own registered AdminModel (its search_fields drive the search).

    		 ()
    inlines Sequence[Inline]

    Related child models listed on this model's detail view (Django TabularInline analog). Each :class:Inline shows the child rows pointing back via its fk_field plus links to the child admin and an "Add" link that pre-fills the parent foreign key.

    		 ()
    lenses Sequence[Lens]

    Named saved list-view presets (Nova-style lenses) rendered as tabs above the list; each applies its filters + ordering via ?lens=<slug>.

    		 ()
    display_timezone str | None

    IANA name of the timezone the operator reads and types datetimes in (for example "America/Sao_Paulo"). None — the default — keeps every datetime in UTC, which is what the columns store.

    Set it and the panel becomes a real widget instead of a raw column editor: the list, the detail view and the edit form render each datetime converted to that zone, and a value typed into the form is read as wall-clock there and stored back in UTC. Without it a TIMESTAMP(timezone=True) column round-trips through an <input type="datetime-local"> that carries no offset at all, so an operator in Brazil types the local hour and the row keeps it as if it were UTC — three hours off, with nothing in the page saying which zone the box meant.

    Only the human-facing views convert. The CSV/JSON export keeps UTC on purpose: it feeds machines, and a timestamp that silently changes meaning between the screen and the file is worse than one that always means the same thing.

    		 None
    password_fields Sequence[FieldRef]

    Columns that take a plaintext password in the form and store its hash.

    		 ()
    password_policy PasswordPolicy | None

    Policy the plaintext must pass. None uses :class:PasswordPolicy defaults.

    		 None
    exclude_fields Sequence[FieldRef]

    Columns the panel never shows or accepts — for a credential that is not a password, like a push subscription's endpoint / p256dh / auth, a device push_token or a totp_secret.

    readonly_fields does not cover that case: it locks the input and still prints the value in the detail view. An excluded column leaves every surface at once — list, detail, create/edit form, CSV import, CSV/JSON export, sortable headers, the parent's inline table and the audit timeline's before/after rows — through :meth:hidden_field_names.

    Hiding the timeline's rows is not enough on its own: the audit table itself would still hold the value. With audit_model set, every excluded column must also be listed in the model's __audit_redact__, which makes the audit write :data:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.db.audit.AUDIT_REDACTED in its place — construction raises otherwise.

    Checked at construction, so a contradiction fails at import time instead of rendering the secret anyway: a name that is not a column, or one that another option also names (list_display, list_filter, search_fields, readonly_fields, upload_fields, autocomplete_fields, password_fields, identity_field, ordering, a lens's filters or order_by), raises ValueError. So does excluding a NOT NULL column with no default while can_create is on: the form could never fill it, and every create would end in Conflict creating <Model>.

    		 ()
    row_scope AdminRowScope | None

    Called with the signed-in principal and this admin on every request that reads or writes a row of :attr:model; the clause it returns is ANDed into every such query — list, count, export, detail, edit, delete, bulk and custom actions, autocomplete and foreign-key options where this model is the target, inlines where it is the child, upload downloads and the CSV import. Return sqlalchemy.true() to leave the rows unrestricted; any value that is not a SQLAlchemy clause — None included — raises :class:AdminRowScopeError (fail closed). A row outside the clause answers 404, the same as a row that does not exist, so the response never confirms it is there. A row the principal creates, edits or imports must still match the clause after the write, or the write is rolled back and refused. For a support role that sees only its own company's rows::

    def own_company(user: UserModel, admin: AdminModel[Any]) -> Any:
    if user.is_superuser:
        return true()
    if user.company_id is None:
        return false()
    return TicketModel.company_id == user.company_id
    		None
    m2m_fields Sequence[FieldRef]

    Many-to-many relationships (relationship(..., secondary=...)) edited on the create/edit form as a multi-select of the target model's rows. The options are the rows the principal reaches through the target admin's row_scope (and need VIEW on it; without it the field is left out and the stored links are kept). Saving replaces the whole set in the same transaction as the row; a link the operator cannot see is kept, and an id outside the options is refused with the "does not exist" error. The detail view lists the linked rows. Checked at construction: a name that is not a relationship with secondary raises ValueError.

    		 ()
    related_counts Sequence[RelatedCount]

    Columns of the list view counting the child rows that reference each row (:class:RelatedCount), one GROUP BY query per page.

    		 ()
    can_duplicate bool

    Show a "Duplicate" button on the detail view that opens the create form filled with the row's values, minus the identity, unique columns, password and upload fields and the audit columns (created_at, updated_at, created_by, updated_by). Needs the column create form (can_create, no create_handler) and CREATE; the source row must be in the principal's scope. The submission is an ordinary create.

    		 False
    bulk_edit_fields Sequence[FieldRef]

    Columns the list's selection can set on every checked row at once ("Edit field"). The value is typed into the column's own widget and validated like the edit form; it is written with one UPDATE ... WHERE id IN (...) AND <scope> in a transaction that is rolled back when the value takes any row out of the scope. A foreign key is checked against the target's scope, and with audit_model one audit entry is written per row. Needs can_edit and EDIT. Each name must be an editable column that is not an upload, password or many-to-many field.

    		 ()
    impersonate AdminImpersonateHandler | None

    Turns a row of this model into a "log in as" target. The detail view gains a button that opens a confirmation page; confirming resolves the account (impersonate_account), records the attempt, calls impersonate(operator, account) (sync or async) and redirects the browser to the URL it returns. Needs AdminPermissionEnum.IMPERSONATE, which make_admin_router never grants without an access_policy; with one, whatever the policy answers for it decides — a deny-list policy ("all but DELETE") grants it too. The row must be inside row_scope. The impersonation is refused when the row or the resolved account is an admin account (:meth:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.admin.AdminAuthBackend.is_admin_account), or when the account's id loads as an admin principal through the backend (a 1:1 profile sharing its primary key with an admin user). Each impersonation is logged at INFO (operator, model, row — never the URL) and, with audit_model set, written there as an event entry before the handler runs. See :func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.admin.make_jwt_impersonation_handler.

    		 None
    impersonate_account AdminImpersonateAccount | None

    Maps the row to the account the handler enters as (lambda profile: profile.user), sync or async; None (default) is the row itself. The admin-account refusal runs on what it returns, and the handler receives it as its second argument. Returning None answers 404.

    		 None
    count_strategy AdminCountStrategy

    How the list counts its rows: "exact" (default), "estimate" or "none". See :class:AdminCountStrategyEnum. The dashboard card of the model follows the same strategy.

    		 EXACT

    editable_field_names ¶

    editable_field_names(
    *, creating: bool = False, instance: ModelT | None = None
) -> list[str]

    Return the columns a create/edit form should expose.

    Excludes the primary key, the audit timestamps (created_at / updated_at), the password hash, the model's __secret_columns__, and any column listed in readonly_fields or exclude_fields — none of which a user edits directly through the generic admin form.

    A secret column that is NOT NULL with no default comes back when creating: the create form starts blank, so it shows no stored value, and without the input no row of a model like BaseWebPushSubscriptionModel could be created through the panel. The edit form, the inline formset and every read surface still leave it out, since those would print the stored value.

    A column named in password_fields is the exception: it comes back in, rendered as a password box that takes plaintext and is hashed on save. Without it no BaseUserModel subclass could be created through the panel at all — the form omitted the column, the insert hit the NOT NULL and the operator read Conflict creating <Model>.

    [Any, "AdminModel[Any]"], "ColumnElement[bool] | Awaitable[ColumnElement[bool]]"
]

    (principal, admin) -> condition: the rows of admin.model the signed-in principal may reach, as a SQLAlchemy boolean clause. Every row is sqlalchemy.true(), said explicitly; None (a forgotten return) is refused with :class:AdminRowScopeError. Sync or async.

    AdminRowScopeError ¶

    Bases: RuntimeError

    A row_scope returned something that is not a SQLAlchemy clause.

    Raised instead of treating the value as "every row": a scope function that forgets its return hands back None, and reading that as unrestricted would open every tenant's rows. The request fails with a 500 and the error is logged with the model name.

    AdminCountStrategyEnum ¶

    Bases: BaseStrEnum

    How the list view counts the rows behind its pagination.

    EXACT runs COUNT(*) on every page, as the list always did. ESTIMATE reads PostgreSQL's planner statistic (pg_class.reltuples) instead, but only while the list shows the whole table: with a search, a filter, a lens or a row_scope clause other than true(), the statistic describes rows the operator is not looking at, so the count is exact again. Other dialects, and a table PostgreSQL never analyzed (reltuples = -1), count exactly too. NONE counts nothing: the list shows only previous / next.

    AdminCountStrategy module-attribute ¶

    AdminCountStrategy = AdminCountStrategyEnum | Literal['exact', 'estimate', 'none']

    What AdminModel(count_strategy=...) takes: the enum or its value.

    AdminImpersonateHandler module-attribute ¶

    AdminImpersonateHandler = Callable[[Any, Any], 'str | Awaitable[str]']

    (operator, account) -> url: where the browser goes to act as account.

    operator is the signed-in admin principal and account what AdminModel(impersonate_account=...) resolved from the row (the row itself by default) — the identity the admin already checked is not an admin account. Sync or async. A handler that enters as anything other than account bypasses that check and must refuse admin accounts itself. The URL usually carries a credential, so the admin never logs it.

    AdminImpersonateAccount module-attribute ¶

    AdminImpersonateAccount = Callable[[Any], 'Any | Awaitable[Any]']

    (row) -> account: the account a row of the model logs in as.

    For impersonate= on a profile model, lambda profile: profile.user. A sync resolver runs inside AsyncSession.run_sync, so it may read a lazy relationship; an async one must load what it reads itself (eager loading, AsyncAttrs.awaitable_attrs). None, an account without id, or one outside the row_scope of its own registered admin answers 404.

    make_jwt_impersonation_handler ¶

    make_jwt_impersonation_handler(
    jwt: JWTUtils, *, redirect_url: str, ttl: timedelta = ADMIN_IMPERSONATION_TTL
) -> AdminImpersonateHandler

    Build an impersonation handler that signs a short access token.

    The token carries sub (the id of the account the admin resolved and checked — see AdminModel(impersonate_account=...)), typ set to :data:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.ACCESS_TOKEN_TYPE — so :func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.make_bearer_token_dependency and :func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.make_jwt_user_dependency accept it like any access token signed with the same secret — the target's email when it has one, and act = {"sub": <operator id>}, the RFC 8693 actor claim, so the app can tell an impersonated session from the user's own and log the operator behind each request (:func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.token_actor reads it back, so a sensitive route can refuse an impersonated session). iat / exp come from :meth:JWTUtils.encode with ttl. The token is otherwise an ordinary access token: every route that accepts the user's own token accepts it.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    jwt JWTUtils

    The helper the app verifies its access tokens with.

    		 required
    redirect_url str

    Where the browser lands, with :data:IMPERSONATION_TOKEN_PLACEHOLDER ({token}) where the token goes, e.g. "https://app.example.com/impersonate#token={token}". A fragment (#) keeps the token out of the app server's access log and out of the Referer the landing page sends.

    		 required
    ttl timedelta

    Token lifetime; defaults to :data:ADMIN_IMPERSONATION_TTL (15 minutes).

    		 ADMIN_IMPERSONATION_TTL

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    AdminImpersonateHandler AdminImpersonateHandler

    The handler to pass as

    ADMIN_IMPERSONATION_EVENT: Final[str] = 'admin.impersonate'

    Event name of the audit entry an impersonation writes.

    Stored in the event column when the audit table mixes in :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.db.audit.AuditRequestMixin, and under context["event"] otherwise.

    ADMIN_IMPERSONATION_FAILED_EVENT module-attribute ¶

    ADMIN_IMPERSONATION_FAILED_EVENT: Final[str] = 'admin.impersonate.failed'

    Event name of the entry written when the handler fails after the attempt.

    The attempt (:data:ADMIN_IMPERSONATION_EVENT) is recorded before the handler runs; this second entry, with the reason in context["reason"], says no credential was handed over.

    IMPERSONATION_TOKEN_PLACEHOLDER module-attribute ¶

    IMPERSONATION_TOKEN_PLACEHOLDER: Final[str] = '{token}'

    Marker :func:make_jwt_impersonation_handler replaces with the token.

    AdminLocale module-attribute ¶

    AdminLocale = Literal['en', 'pt-BR']

    A language the admin catalog ships.

    ADMIN_LOCALES module-attribute ¶

    ADMIN_LOCALES: Final[tuple[AdminLocale, ...]] = ('en', 'pt-BR')

    Every locale in :data:ADMIN_MESSAGES, the default first.

    DEFAULT_ADMIN_LOCALE module-attribute ¶

    DEFAULT_ADMIN_LOCALE: Final[AdminLocale] = 'en'

    Locale of an AdminSite built without locale=.

    {locale: {key: template}}; templates use str.format placeholders.

    admin_text ¶

    admin_text(locale: str, key: str, /, **params: Any) -> str

    Return the catalog text for key in locale.

    A key missing from locale falls back to English, and one missing from both to the key itself, so a gap renders something readable instead of failing the page; tests/test_admin_i18n_guard.py keeps both languages complete, so neither fallback is reached by the SDK's own keys.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    locale str

    One of :data:ADMIN_LOCALES.

    		 required
    key str

    The catalog key, such as "list.apply".

    		 required
    **params Any

    Values for the template's {placeholders}.

    		 {}

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    str str

    The formatted text.

    admin_plural ¶

    admin_plural(locale: str, key: str, count: int, /, **params: Any) -> str

    Reads <key>.one when count is 1 and <key>.other otherwise — the rule both shipped languages follow — and passes count to the template along with params.

    ADMIN_IMPORT_MAX_BYTES module-attribute ¶

    ADMIN_IMPORT_MAX_BYTES: Final[int] = 512 * 1024

    Largest CSV, in bytes, the import page accepts.

    The preview carries the whole file to the confirmation as one signed hidden field, so the cap also bounds that request. Measured over six files of 512 KiB (random hex, random printable ASCII, random Latin-1, random CJK, random emoji, one-character lines), the signed field came to at most 571 099 bytes — random printable ASCII, which compresses least — under the 1 MiB Starlette allows one multipart field (max_part_size).

    ADMIN_IMPORT_PREVIEW_MAX_AGE_SECONDS module-attribute ¶

    ADMIN_IMPORT_PREVIEW_MAX_AGE_SECONDS: Final[int] = 3600

    How long a preview can be confirmed before the file must be sent again.

    ADMIN_IMPORT_PREVIEW_ROWS module-attribute ¶

    ADMIN_IMPORT_PREVIEW_ROWS: Final[int] = 20

    Rows of the file shown in the preview table; the counts cover all of them.

    Inline ¶

    Inline(
    model: type[BaseModel],
    fk_field: FieldRef,
    *,
    list_display: Sequence[FieldRef] | None = None,
    label: str | None = None,
    editable: bool = False,
    can_delete: bool = False,
)

    A related child model surfaced on the parent's detail view.

    Django's TabularInline analog: the detail view of the parent lists the child rows that point back at it (via fk_field) as a compact table, with a link to each child's own admin and an "Add" link that pre-fills the parent foreign key. The child model must have its own registered :class:AdminModel for the links to work (the inline reuses the child admin's list_display and CRUD routes); without it, the rows still render read-only.

    When editable is set, the same rows render as an in-place formset (one row of inputs per child, plus one blank row to add another) posting back to the parent's detail view — no navigation to the child admin. Editing an inline requires the child model to have its own registered :class:AdminModel (the formset reuses its editable fields, minus upload/autocomplete columns, which stay on the child's own form) and that admin's can_edit; can_delete adds a per-row delete checkbox (gated on the child admin's can_delete).

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    model type[BaseModel]

    The child model class.
    fk_field str

    The child column that references the parent.
    list_display list[str] | None

    Columns to show; falls back to the child admin's list_display (or every column).
    label str | None

    Section heading; defaults to the model name.
    editable bool

    Render the rows as an editable in-place formset.
    can_delete bool

    Show a per-row delete checkbox (editable only).

    Build the inline config. See class docstring.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    model type[BaseModel]

    The child model class.

    		 required
    fk_field FieldRef

    The child column referencing the parent.

    		 required
    list_display Sequence[FieldRef] | None

    Columns to show.

    		 None
    label str | None

    Section heading.

    		 None
    editable bool

    Render an in-place editable formset instead of a read-only table.

    		 False
    can_delete bool

    Add a per-row delete checkbox (only when editable and the child admin allows deletion).

    		 False

    Raises:

    Type Description
    TypeError

    When model is not a BaseModel subclass.

    Lens ¶

    Lens(
    name: str,
    *,
    filters: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    order_by: str | None = None,
    label: str | None = None,
)

    A named, saved list-view preset (Nova-style lens).

    A lens bundles a set of filters and an optional ordering under a label. On the list view lenses render as tabs; clicking one applies its filters (ANDed with the user's search/filters) and ordering. A "support triage" lens might pin {"status": "open", "priority__gte": 3} sorted by oldest-first, so an operator reaches the working set in one click instead of re-entering filters.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    name str

    The lens identifier; its slug (lowercased, spaces→hyphens) is the ?lens= value.
    filters dict[str, Any]

    Column name to the value the tab's rows must match, ANDed into the query, e.g. {"user_id": 1234, "is_active": True}. A list is IN, None is IS NULL, and a <column>__<op> key applies an operator ({"price__gte": 10}); every convention is listed on :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.BaseRepository. An unknown column or operator makes :class:AdminModel raise ValueError at construction.
    order_by str | None

    Column to order by; -col for descending. Applied unless the user clicked a column sort.
    label str | None

    Tab label; defaults to name.

    Build a lens. See class docstring.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    name str

    The lens identifier.

    		 required

A list is IN, None is IS NULL, and a <column>__<op> key applies an operator ({"price__gte": 10}); every convention is listed on :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.BaseRepository. An unknown column or operator makes :class:AdminModel raise ValueError at construction.

    		 None
    order_by str | None

    Ordering column (-col = desc).

    		 None

    RelatedCount ¶

    RelatedCount(fk: InstrumentedAttribute[Any], *, label: str | None = None)

    A list-view column counting the child rows that point at each row.

    Declared on the parent admin with the child's foreign-key column (RelatedCount(OrderModel.user_id, label="Orders") on the users admin). The list renders one extra column holding, per row, how many child rows reference it. The counts of a page come from one SELECT fk, COUNT(*) ... WHERE fk IN (<page ids>) GROUP BY fk, never one query per row, and that query carries the child admin's row_scope, so the number covers only the children the principal reaches.

    When the child model has its own registered :class:AdminModel and the principal may VIEW it, the count links to the child's list filtered by the parent (?filter_<fk>=<id>). A child the principal may not VIEW drops the column altogether: the number is that model's data, whichever page shows it. A child with no registered admin is asked through a throwaway AdminModel(child), like an :class:Inline, and renders the count without a link.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    model type[BaseModel]

    The child model, read from the column.
    fk_field str

    The child column that references the parent.
    label str | None

    Column heading; defaults to the child's plural name.
    target_table str

    The parent table the column references.
    target_column str

    The parent column it references (id).

    Build the related count. See class docstring.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    fk InstrumentedAttribute[Any]

    The child's foreign-key column, as a mapped attribute (OrderModel.user_id) so the child model is known.

    		 required
    label str | None

    Column heading.

    		 None

    Raises:

    Type Description
    TypeError

    When fk is not a mapped column attribute of a BaseModel subclass.
    ValueError

    When the column carries no ForeignKey.

    AdminPermissionEnum ¶

    Bases: BaseStrEnum

    An admin action gated by an :data:AdminAccessPolicy.

    IMPERSONATE (entering the app as a row of a model declared with AdminModel(impersonate=...)) is the one permission that is not granted when make_admin_router runs without an access_policy: acting as another account reaches past the admin's own screens. With a policy, whatever it answers for IMPERSONATE decides — a deny-list policy ("everything but DELETE") grants it as well.

    AdminAccessPolicy = Callable[
    [Any, "AdminModel[Any]", AdminPermissionEnum], bool | Awaitable[bool]
]

    AdminActionPolicy = Callable[
    [Any, "AdminModel[Any]", "AdminAction"], bool | Awaitable[bool]
]

    Bases: BaseStrEnum

    An admin panel that is not about one model.

    Gated by an :data:AdminSurfacePolicy instead of the per-model :data:AdminAccessPolicy, since there is no :class:AdminModel to ask about.

    Threshold(green: float, yellow: float, lower_is_better: bool = False)

    Green / yellow / red bands for one numeric indicator.

    With lower_is_better=False (the default) a value at or above green is green, at or above yellow is yellow, and below yellow is red. With lower_is_better=True the comparison flips: at or below green is green, at or below yellow is yellow, above yellow is red — "messages until the user found the route" is good when it is small.     admin_action ¶

    admin_action(
    *,
    label: str,
    name: str | None = None,
    dangerous: bool = False,
    schema: type[BaseModel] | None = None,
) -> Callable[[_HandlerT], _HandlerT]

    Mark an async function as a custom admin action.

    The decorated function is registered by passing it to AdminModel(actions=[...]); the decorator only attaches metadata, so the function stays directly callable (and unit-testable) on its own.

    The panel commits the request session after the handler returns, with or without secrets in the result, and rolls it back when the handler raises.

    With schema, picking the action on the list opens a form generated from the model, with the selected ids carried along; the handler runs only on a valid submission, as handler(data, ctx). An invalid one re-renders the form with 400, and an :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.AppException from the handler rolls the session back and re-renders it with the message. The form carries a single-use nonce, so resubmitting the same form does not run the action again.

    schema type[BaseModel] | None

    The input asked before the action runs (a reason, an amount, a date).

    AdminActionResult dataclass ¶

    AdminActionResult(
    message: str, category: str = "success", secrets: Sequence[AdminSecret] = ()
)

    The outcome of a custom action.

    Without secrets the message is flashed on the list view, carried by the redirect's query string. With secrets the panel answers the action's own POST with a page that shows the message and each secret once — no redirect, so no value reaches a URL, the browser history, an access log or a Referer — sent with Cache-Control: no-store and Referrer-Policy: no-referrer. The request's database session is committed before that page renders, so a secret on screen is never one whose row was rolled back.

    Name Type Description

    Banner style — "success" (default), "error" or "warning".

    AdminCreateHandler dataclass ¶

    AdminCreateHandler(
    schema: type[BaseModel], handler: CreateHandlerFunc, label: str | None = None
)

    A create flow driven by a schema and a service, not by the columns.

    Some rows are born from a service rather than typed in: an API key is a generated secret stored as a hash and shown in plaintext once, so the column form (key_hash, key_prefix typed by hand) is wrong for it. Pass this as AdminModel(create_handler=...) and the list's "+ New" button opens a form generated from :attr:schema; on submit the panel validates it and calls :attr:handler.

    The handler returns the same :class:AdminActionResult a custom action does. With secrets, the database session is committed and the values are shown once on the POST's own response; reloading that page does not call the handler again (a single-use nonce in the form). Without them, the panel redirects to the list and flashes the message. An :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.AppException raised by the handler re-renders the form with its message and what was typed.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    schema type[BaseModel]

    The Pydantic model the form is generated from and the submission is validated against. A field whose name is in the admin's autocomplete_fields renders as the same foreign-key search box.
    handler CreateHandlerFunc

    The async function that creates the record.
    label str | None

    Text of the "+ New" button and the form heading; None uses New <verbose name>.

    manual_payout_admin ¶

    manual_payout_admin(
    model: type[BaseManualPayoutModel],
    *,
    upload_storage: UploadStorage,
    ledger_factory: Callable[[AsyncSession], WalletLedger] | None = None,
    hooks: ManualPayoutHooks | None = None,
    audit_model: type[BaseAuditLogModel] | None = None,
    display_timezone: str | None = None,
    verbose_name: str = "Saque manual",
    verbose_name_plural: str = "Saques manuais",
    actions: Sequence[ActionHandler] = (),
) -> AdminModel[Any]

    Configure the panel for a manual payout table.

    • list filtered by status (a select labelled Pendente / Pago / Cancelado / Recusado), searchable by correlation_id;
    • no "Activate" / "Deactivate" bulk actions, and is_active read-only: a payout is never switched off;
    • every money column read-only — amount, user, key, correlation id, status, end-to-end id and who completed or refused it; no create, no delete, no import;
    • receipt_key an upload that takes only a PDF (declared type application/pdf and bytes starting %PDF-), downloadable from the row's page, and refused once the row is no longer PENDING;
    • rejection_reason editable while the row is PENDING; on a final row it leaves the edit form and a posted value is ignored (readonly_fields_for);
    • the "Marcar como pago" action (:func:make_mark_paid_action), and, with ledger_factory, "Recusar e devolver" (:func:make_reject_action).

    Name Type Description Default
    model type[BaseManualPayoutModel]

    The project's concrete model.

    		 required
    upload_storage UploadStorage

    Where receipts are stored.

    ledger_factory Callable[[AsyncSession], WalletLedger] | None

    Builds the wallet ledger on the panel's session. None leaves the "refuse and refund" action out.

    		 None
    hooks ManualPayoutHooks | None

    Callbacks run inside each transition — the same instance the provider gets.

    		 None
    audit_model type[BaseAuditLogModel] | None

    Shows the row's change timeline when set.

    		 None
    display_timezone str | None

    IANA zone for the datetimes.

    		 None
    verbose_name str

    Singular name in the panel.

    		 'Saque manual'
    verbose_name_plural str

    Plural name in the panel.

    		 'Saques manuais'
    actions Sequence[ActionHandler]

    AdminModel[Any]: Ready for site.register.

    AdminAuthBackend ¶

    Bases: ABC, Generic[PrincipalT]

    Abstract base for admin authentication.

    Implementations receive a session-bound async DB session per login attempt; the default :class:UserModelAuthBackend queries a :class:BaseUserModel subclass and enforces is_admin=True. Custom backends can use the same protocol to integrate LDAP, OAuth, IAM tokens, etc.

    The class is generic in the principal — the value authenticate returns and every other method consumes. Parameterizing it is what makes that contract checkable::

    class LdapAuthBackend(AdminAuthBackend[LdapEntry]):
    def display_name(self, principal: LdapEntry) -> str:
        return principal.common_name

    Subclassing without a parameter stays valid and resolves to AdminAuthBackend[Any], which is the behaviour that shipped before the class was generic — nothing has to change to keep working.

The default reads a truthy is_admin attribute, which is what :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.BaseUserModel carries; override it when admin access is decided by something else (a role column, a group).

    load_account async ¶

    load_account(session: AsyncSession, account_id: str) -> PrincipalT | None

    Load the account with account_id without any sign-in filter.

    :meth:is_admin_identity asks :meth:is_admin_account about what this returns, so an admin that :meth:load_principal drops — inactive, revoked, missing MFA — is still recognised as an admin. The default returns None (the base class does not know where accounts live); a backend whose :meth:load_principal filters should override it. The account is the same kind of object the backend signs in, only without the sign-in filter.

    is_admin_identity async ¶

    is_admin_identity(session: AsyncSession, account_id: str) -> bool

    Whether account_id names an account that can use the admin.

    The impersonation flow asks this about the id that goes into the credential, on top of :meth:is_admin_account on the row, so a model whose rows share their primary key with the user table (a 1:1 profile) cannot hand out an admin's identity. The default answers True when :meth:load_principal finds a principal for that id, or when :meth:load_account returns an account :meth:is_admin_account calls an admin. A custom backend whose load_principal filters (inactive, MFA) must override :meth:load_account or this method, or such an admin passes.

    credential_fingerprint ¶

    credential_fingerprint(principal: PrincipalT) -> str | None

    Return a value that changes whenever the principal's credential does.

    The admin router stores a keyed digest of it in the session cookie at sign-in and compares it on every request, so changing the password (or whatever the fingerprint covers) ends every session issued before the change. Defaults to None: the session is not bound to any credential, which suits backends whose credential the SDK cannot see (LDAP, OAuth). Override to opt in.

    UserModelAuthBackend ¶

    UserModelAuthBackend(
    user_model: type[BaseUserModel],
    *,

    Bases: AdminAuthBackend[BaseUserModel]

    Default backend backed by :class:BaseUserModel.

    Authenticates by selecting the row whose email matches the inbound identifier (case-insensitive), verifying the password via :class:tempest_fastapi_sdk.PasswordUtils and enforcing both is_admin=True and is_active=True. The :attr:last_login_at column is stamped on every successful login.

    Who counts as an admin is :meth:is_authorized — is_admin by default. A service that authorizes by its own role column overrides that one method instead of re-implementing :meth:authenticate and :meth:load_principal, which is where the timing-safe password check lives.

    		 1
    require_mfa bool

    Refuse /admin to an account without MFA enrolled (:meth:mfa_enabled). Login answers "MFA enrollment required for /admin" (401, on the login page) — only after the password is right, like the other account checks — and :meth:load_principal drops the session of an account whose MFA was turned off after it signed in. The admin has no enrollment screen: enrollment happens out of band, through the /auth/mfa/enroll + /auth/mfa/confirm routes of :func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.make_auth_router or tempest user create --require-mfa on the CLI. Default False: MFA is asked for only from accounts that enrolled.

    authenticate async ¶

    authenticate(session: AsyncSession, *, identifier: str, password: str) -> BaseUserModel

    Verify credentials against the configured user model.

    The password is checked before anything about the account is revealed. An unknown address pays a bcrypt check against a throwaway hash (:meth:PasswordUtils.dummy_verify, on one instance kept by the backend so the hash is built once, not per attempt), and every wrong password — unknown, non-admin, disabled or admin account — is refused with the same "Invalid credentials". Only a caller who already knows the password learns that the account is disabled, not authorized (:meth:is_authorized) or, under require_mfa=True, missing MFA enrollment. Checking is_active and is_admin first let anyone with a list of addresses read which ones are admins, and which are disabled, off the error message and the response time.

    make_admin_router ¶

    make_admin_router(
    site: AdminSite,
    *,
    db: AsyncDatabaseManager,
    auth_backend: AdminAuthBackend[Any],
    secret_key: str,
    prefix: str = "/admin",
    session_store: SessionStore | None = None,
    cookie_secure: bool = True,
    export_max_rows: int = 5000,
    show_metrics: bool = True,
    show_logs: bool = False,
    log_dir: str | Path = "logs",
    access_policy: AdminAccessPolicy | None = None,
    action_policy: AdminActionPolicy | None = None,
    surface_policy: AdminSurfacePolicy | None = None,
    sql_shell: SqlShellService | None = None,
    tasks: TaskPanelService[Any] | None = None,
    storage: StorageBrowserService | None = None,
    mfa_throttle: AttemptThrottle | None = None,
    login_throttle: AttemptThrottle | Literal[False] | None = None,
    login_ip_throttle: AttemptThrottle | Literal[False] | None = None,
    trusted_ip_header: str | None = None,
    session_revocations: AdminSessionRevocations | None = None,
    search_results_per_model: int = ADMIN_SEARCH_RESULTS_PER_MODEL,
) -> APIRouter

    Build the FastAPI router that mounts the admin site.

    Routes attached:

    • GET {prefix}/login — login form.
    • POST {prefix}/login — login submit.
    • POST {prefix}/logout — clear session + redirect.
    • GET/POST {prefix}/mfa — TOTP challenge for MFA-enabled principals (between the password step and full access).
    • GET {prefix}/ — dashboard listing registered admins.
    • GET {prefix}/logs — structured application logs (when show_logs=True).
    • GET {prefix}/m/{slug}/ — list view (paginated, sortable, filterable).
    • GET {prefix}/m/{slug}/export.{fmt} — CSV/JSON export of the current (filtered + sorted) result set.
    • POST {prefix}/m/{slug}/bulk — bulk delete / activate / deactivate, or a custom action, on the selected rows; a custom action declared with schema= answers its input form first.
    • GET/POST {prefix}/m/{slug}/new — create form + submit (when can_create).
    • GET {prefix}/m/{slug}/{identity} — detail view.
    • GET/POST {prefix}/m/{slug}/{identity}/edit — edit form + submit (when can_edit).
    • POST {prefix}/m/{slug}/{identity}/delete — delete row (when can_delete).
    • GET/POST {prefix}/m/{slug}/{identity}/impersonate — confirm and enter the app as the row (when AdminModel(impersonate=...)).
    • GET {prefix}/m/{slug}/{identity}/restore/{entry_id} — the edit form pre-filled with the values an audit entry replaced (when audit_model and can_edit).
    • GET {prefix}/search — global search across every model with search_fields.
    • Static files under {prefix}/static named admin_static.
    • GET {prefix}/_ssr/htmx.js — the HTMX bundled in the SDK (ssr/_static/htmx.min.js), served without a session because the login page loads it too. No admin page fetches a script from a third-party host.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    site AdminSite

    The configured registry.

    		 required
    db AsyncDatabaseManager

    Active DB manager (used for both sessions and the readiness check).

    		 required
    auth_backend AdminAuthBackend[Any]

    Backend resolving login credentials to a principal.

    		 required
    secret_key str

    Secret used to sign the session cookie. 32 bytes minimum.

    		 required
    prefix str

    URL prefix; defaults to "/admin".

    		 '/admin'
    session_store SessionStore | None

    Override the default :class:SignedCookieSessionStore.

    		 None
    cookie_secure bool

    Set the Secure flag on cookies. Default True; disable only for local HTTP dev.

    		 True
    export_max_rows int

    Hard cap on rows returned by the CSV/JSON export endpoint. Exports beyond this are truncated (a header/log notes it) to bound memory.

    		 5000
    show_metrics bool

    When True (default), the dashboard renders a CPU/RAM/disk panel via MetricsUtils — silently omitted when the [metrics] extra is not installed. Set False to skip the per-request sample entirely.

    		 True
    show_logs bool

    When True, a GET {prefix}/logs page is mounted and a "Logs" entry appears in the sidebar. It reads the structured JSON files written by configure_logging (see log_dir) and renders them filtered + paginated. Defaults to False (opt-in — log payloads expose tracebacks and request metadata).

    		 False
    log_dir str | Path

    Directory holding the structured log files, matching the log_dir passed to configure_logging. Only consulted when show_logs is True. Defaults to "logs". When the directory has no log files yet the page renders an empty state.

    		 'logs'
    access_policy AdminAccessPolicy | None

    Optional granular RBAC hook asked (principal, admin, AdminPermissionEnum) for every model action. None (default) allows everything (subject to the AdminModel.can_* flags). A policy that denies an action yields 403 and hides the model from the dashboard + nav for VIEW. Composes with the can_* flags — both must allow. It also governs what a page renders of another model: inline tables need VIEW on the child (an editable inline's add row CREATE, its delete box DELETE), and foreign-key selects, list filters and autocomplete need VIEW on the referenced admin.

    		 None
    action_policy AdminActionPolicy | None

    Hook asked (principal, admin, AdminAction) before a custom action runs and when the list builds its action menu. When set, a custom action needs VIEW on the model (access_policy) and this policy's approval, and no longer EDIT: one action can be granted without the edit form, and one role can run an action another cannot. A denied action is left out of the menu and its POST answers 403. None (default) keeps asking EDIT for every custom action.

    		 None
    surface_policy AdminSurfacePolicy | None

    Hook asked (principal, AdminSurfaceEnum) before the SQL console, the task panel (cancel included) or the logs page (export included) is served; a denial yields 403 and drops the sidebar entry. None (default) allows every surface when access_policy is also None, and denies every surface once an access_policy is configured: a principal restricted to some models would otherwise read any table through the console. Pass one to grant the surfaces to the roles that should have them.

    		 None
    sql_shell SqlShellService | None

    When given, mounts the SQL console at GET/POST {prefix}/sql and adds its nav entry.

    		 None
    tasks TaskPanelService[Any] | None

    When given, mounts the task panel at GET {prefix}/tasks (declared schedule + persisted runs), the run detail at GET {prefix}/tasks/{job_id} and the cancel action at POST {prefix}/tasks/{job_id}/cancel, and adds its nav entry. Either half of the service may be absent; a section with no source is not rendered.

    		 None
    storage StorageBrowserService | None

    When given, mounts the storage browser at GET {prefix}/storage (folder listing), GET {prefix}/storage/object (one object: metadata, preview, text editor), GET {prefix}/storage/raw (the bytes, inline only for inline-safe types) and the POST writes under {prefix}/storage/ (upload, replace, edit, rename, delete), and adds its nav entry. A read_only service answers 403 to every write.

    		 None
    mfa_throttle AttemptThrottle | None

    Failure budget for the POST {prefix}/mfa challenge, keyed on the principal, so a fresh password login does not reset it. Once spent, the challenge answers 429 with Retry-After before the code is checked; a correct code resets the key. None (default) allows ADMIN_MFA_THROTTLE_MAX_ATTEMPTS (5) wrong codes per ADMIN_MFA_THROTTLE_WINDOW_SECONDS (900) on an :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.InMemoryThrottleBackend, which counts per process: behind more than one worker, pass an :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.AttemptThrottle on Redis.

    		 None
    login_throttle AttemptThrottle | Literal[False] | None

    Failure budget for POST {prefix}/login per identifier, keyed "login:<sha256 of the normalized identifier>" (:func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.login_throttle_key, the key make_auth_router uses). Each attempt reserves one unit before the password is checked and a successful login clears the key, so only failures accumulate; the attempt past max_attempts re-renders the login page with 429 and Retry-After whatever the password, so the response is no oracle. Spent the same way for an identifier with no account. None (default) allows ADMIN_LOGIN_THROTTLE_MAX_ATTEMPTS (5) per ADMIN_LOGIN_THROTTLE_WINDOW_SECONDS (900) on an :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.InMemoryThrottleBackend — per process, so pass one on Redis behind more than one worker. False turns it off.

    		 None
    login_ip_throttle AttemptThrottle | Literal[False] | None

    Failure budget for POST {prefix}/login per client IP ("admin-login-ip:<addr>"), for one source trying many identifiers. Read before the identifier budget is spent and counted only on a refused login; a success does not clear it, since one valid account would otherwise reset the counter between guesses. None (default) turns it on with ADMIN_LOGIN_IP_THROTTLE_MAX_ATTEMPTS (20) per 900 s in memory only when trusted_ip_header is set, and leaves it off otherwise: behind a reverse proxy without that header every operator shares the proxy's address, and twenty bad logins from anyone would lock all of them out. A throttle passed explicitly always applies. False turns it off.

    		 None
    trusted_ip_header str | None

    Single edge-set header holding the real client IP (e.g. "x-real-ip") for login_ip_throttle. None uses the transport peer. See :func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.get_client_ip.

    		 None
    session_revocations AdminSessionRevocations | None

    Where POST {prefix}/logout marks the session it ends; every request refuses a marked session, so a copy of the cookie stops working at logout instead of at max_age. None (default) keeps the marks on an :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.InMemoryThrottleBackend for the store's max_age_seconds — per process, so behind more than one worker pass AdminSessionRevocations(redis_client). Independently of this, the session is bound to :meth:AdminAuthBackend.credential_fingerprint, so a password change ends every session issued before it, on every replica.

    		 None
    search_results_per_model int

    Rows the global search lists per model. Defaults to :data:ADMIN_SEARCH_RESULTS_PER_MODEL (5).

    		 ADMIN_SEARCH_RESULTS_PER_MODEL

    Returns:

    Name Type Description

    A router ready to attach via app.include_router.

    Raises:

    When the [admin] extra is not installed, so Jinja2 is unavailable to render the templates.
    ValueError

    AdminSessionRevocations ¶

    AdminSessionRevocations(
    backend: ThrottleBackend, *, ttl_seconds: int = ADMIN_SESSION_MAX_AGE_SECONDS
)

    Server-side list of admin sessions ended by logout.

    The default admin cookie is stateless: clearing it on logout only asks the browser to forget it, and a copy taken earlier would keep working until max_age. POST /logout therefore marks the session's :attr:AdminSession.session_id here, and every request checks the mark before trusting the cookie. A mark lives as long as the cookie could, then expires on its own.

    Storage is any :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.utils.throttle.ThrottleBackend — the same shape redis.asyncio.Redis and :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.utils.throttle.InMemoryThrottleBackend have. The in-memory one is per process: behind more than one worker or replica, pass the Redis client so a logout served by one is seen by all.

    AdminSubmissionNonces ¶

    AdminSubmissionNonces(backend: ThrottleBackend, *, ttl_seconds: int)

    Single-use tokens that stop a reloaded POST from running twice.

    A form whose answer is the POST itself — the page that shows a new API key once — is resubmitted by the browser on reload, and before #739 that ran the handler again and minted a second key. Each such form now carries a nonce (:meth:issue); the POST calls :meth:consume before running, and only the first call for a nonce gets True.

    consume is one incr on the same :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.utils.throttle.ThrottleBackend the session revocations use, so the check is atomic and, with the Redis client passed to :class:AdminSessionRevocations, shared across workers. With the default in-memory backend it is per process: a resend that lands on another worker runs again.

    SignedCookieSessionStore ¶

    SignedCookieSessionStore(
    secret_key: str,
    *,
    cookie_name: str = "tempest_admin",
    max_age_seconds: int = ADMIN_SESSION_MAX_AGE_SECONDS,
    secure: bool = True,
    same_site: SameSite = "lax",
    path: str = "/admin",
)

    Bases: SessionStore

    Default session store using a single signed JSON cookie.

    The cookie is signed with HMAC-SHA256 via :mod:itsdangerous so tampered payloads are rejected. Cookies are scoped to HttpOnly + SameSite=Lax and may be flagged Secure for HTTPS deployments; signed payloads also carry their own expiration via the max_age argument passed to loads.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    secret_key str

    Shared secret used to sign the cookie. MUST be at least 32 bytes; production deployments should source it from a secrets manager.

    		 required
    cookie_name str

    Cookie name. Defaults to "tempest_admin".

    		 'tempest_admin'
    max_age_seconds int

    Session lifetime; cookies older than this are rejected by :meth:load.

    		 ADMIN_SESSION_MAX_AGE_SECONDS
    secure bool

    Whether to flag the cookie Secure. Default True — disable in local-only HTTP setups.

    		 True
    same_site SameSite

    SameSite policy — "lax" (default), "strict" or "none", matched ignoring case and stored lower-cased.

    		 'lax'
    path str

    Cookie path. Defaults to "/admin".

    		 '/admin'

    AdminLoginCSRF ¶

    AdminLoginCSRF(
    secret_key: str,
    *,
    secure: bool = True,
    path: str = "/admin",
    max_age_seconds: int = ADMIN_LOGIN_CSRF_MAX_AGE_SECONDS,
)

    CSRF token for the login form, which runs before any session exists.

    Every other admin form checks the token stored in the session. The login form cannot: there is no session yet, and without a token a page on another site could make an operator's browser post the attacker's credentials to /login — the response sets the admin cookie, and the operator ends up working in the attacker's account (login CSRF). SameSite=Lax does not prevent it: it restricts which cookies a cross-site POST sends, not the cookie its response sets.

    The token is random, signed with a timestamp into a short-lived cookie scoped to the admin prefix, and repeated in a hidden form field; the submit compares the two in constant time. A cross-site page cannot read the cookie, so it cannot fill the field.

    Independent of the configured :class:SessionStore, so a deployment that swaps the store keeps the protection.

    Initialize the signer.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    secret_key str

    The admin signing key; at least 32 bytes, the rule :class:SignedCookieSessionStore applies.

    		 required
    secure bool

    Whether to flag the cookie Secure.

    		 True
    path str

    Cookie path scope — the admin prefix.

    		 '/admin'
    max_age_seconds int

    How long a rendered form stays valid.

    		 ADMIN_LOGIN_CSRF_MAX_AGE_SECONDS

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValueError

    When secret_key is empty or too short.
    ImportError

    When the [admin] extra is not installed.

    BRLocationMap dataclass ¶

    BRLocationMap(
    title: str,
    model: type[BRLocationMixin],
    *,
    where: Callable[[], ColumnElement[bool]] | None = None,
    city_limit: int = 50,
    value_label: str = "users",
)

    A map page of where a model's rows are in Brazil.

    title and model are positional; the rest is keyword-only.

    The page needs VIEW on the model under the access_policy (it shows the model's data, aggregated), asked of the model's registered :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.admin.AdminModel or, when the model is not registered, of a throwaway AdminModel(model).

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    title str

    The page heading and the sidebar label.
    model type[BRLocationMixin]

    A model with :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.geo.BRLocationMixin.
    where Callable[[], ColumnElement[bool]] | None

    Builds an extra filter for every count (lambda: UserModel.is_active.is_(True)); a callable, so the expression is built per request.
    city_limit int

    How many cities the bubbles and the table show, largest first.
    value_label str

    Word after each number in the tooltips and the tables ("usuários").
    slug str

    The URL segment, derived from title.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    TypeError

    When model does not have the mixin's columns.
    ValueError

    When city_limit is below 1, or title yields an empty slug.

    AdminTheme dataclass ¶

    AdminTheme(
    accent: str = "#2563eb",
    accent_hover: str = "#1d4ed8",
    danger: str = "#b91c1c",
    header_bg: str = DEFAULT_HEADER_BG,
    sidebar_bg: str | None = None,
    header_fg: str | None = None,
    page_bg: str | None = None,
    radius: str = "8px",
    font_family: str | None = None,
    logo_url: str | None = None,
    logo_alt: str = "Logo",
    favicon_url: str | None = None,
    footer_text: str = "Powered by tempest-fastapi-sdk",
    dark_mode: bool = False,
    custom_css_url: str | None = None,
)

    Typed appearance overrides for the admin panel.

    Every field maps to a CSS custom property on :root (or to a piece of chrome like the logo / footer). All fields have sensible defaults that reproduce the stock look, so AdminTheme() is a no-op and you only set what you want to change.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    accent str

    Primary accent color — links, primary buttons, active sidebar item. Any CSS color ("#7c3aed", "rebeccapurple", "rgb(124 58 237)").
    accent_hover str

    Hover/active shade of :attr:accent.
    danger str

    Color for destructive actions and error messages.
    header_bg str

    Background of the top header band. Light by default; the header and sidebar text switch to light on a dark hex value on their own.
    sidebar_bg str | None

    Background of the left sidebar. Falls back to :attr:header_bg when None so the chrome reads as one surface.
    header_fg str | None

    Text color on the header and sidebar. None picks dark or light text from the luminance of :attr:header_bg / :attr:sidebar_bg; set it when the background is not a hex value and the guess is wrong.
    page_bg str | None

    Main content background. None uses the mode default (light grey, or near-black when :attr:dark_mode is on).
    radius str

    Border-radius applied to buttons, inputs, cards and tables ("8px", "0.75rem", "0" for square).
    font_family str | None

    CSS font-family for the whole panel. None keeps the system font stack.
    logo_url str | None

    URL of an image shown in the header instead of the brand text. None shows the text brand.
    logo_alt str

    alt text for the logo image.
    favicon_url str | None

    URL of the browser-tab favicon. None lets the browser use its default.
    footer_text str

    Text shown in the page footer.
    dark_mode bool

    When True, the content surfaces (page background, cards, text, table rows, inputs, borders) switch to a dark palette, and so does the chrome while :attr:header_bg is the default. :attr:accent and the other colors still apply.
    custom_css_url str | None

    URL of an extra stylesheet linked after the theme, so it overrides everything. The escape hatch for anything the typed fields do not cover.

    css_variables ¶

    css_variables() -> dict[str, str]

    Return the :root custom properties this theme sets.

    Returns:

    Type Description
    dict[str, str]

    dict[str, str]: Mapping of CSS variable name to value. Only
    dict[str, str]

    the always-present variables are included here; mode- and
    dict[str, str]

    font-dependent rules are emitted by :meth:to_css.

    to_css ¶

    to_css() -> str

    Render the full <style> body for this theme.

    Combines the :meth:css_variables :root block with the optional dark-mode surface overrides. The result is injected verbatim inside a <style> element in the page <head>.

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    str str

    CSS text. Empty-safe — a default AdminTheme() still
    str

    returns a valid (no-op-equivalent) block.
    Notes

    The dark surface block covers the content area; the chrome goes dark through :meth:css_variables (--tempest-bg). The block is skipped entirely when the project pinned its own page_bg — an explicit value always wins.
